TEAM DESCRIPTION

Team CyberNex HIT is on a mission to build next-generation tech solutions. Leveraging our background in Computer Science and systems programming, we approach problem-solving with a security-first mindset. By combining efficient development practices with core engineering principles, we aim to turn complex challenges into accessible, high-impact applications.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots
summary:
Enviro Sense turns NASA FIRMS satellite fire data and a live ground sensor into an early wildfire warning system.

The challenge: fires spread faster than warnings reach people, MODIS and VIIRS detections come at different resolutions, and nothing watches the ground between satellite passes.

What we built: we download MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections from NASA FIRMS, clean them, and merge them onto one 1 km grid. This gives a burning-activity calendar for any area in South Asia since 2020 (about 1.98 million grid-cell records), flags unusual days, and gives a 14-day fire-risk outlook from past seasons and recent activity.

A Raspberry Pi node sends readings every 5 seconds to our Node.js server. In this prototype the Pi simulates temperature, humidity and smoke values; we also document a real design using DHT22 and MQ-2 sensors. The server watches the trend, labels each reading NORMAL, WARNING or FIRE, and automatically emails registered users within 100 km and texts verified residents within 1 km. An AI model rewrites the briefing, and a checker stops it from inventing facts.

Why it matters: earlier, clearer warnings give people time to act. The demo is free to use on any device.
details:
What it does

Enviro Sense is an early-warning system for fires. It combines two sources. NASA satellites show where and when burning has happened and what the next 14 days are likely to look like. A Raspberry Pi sensor node (temperature, humidity and smoke) shows what is happening right now at one place. When the sensor sees a fire may be starting, the server automatically warns people within 1 km by text message and phone call, and warns people within 100 km by email. Twice a month, on the 1st and 15th, an AI agent sends everyone nearby a safety circular. It has a month-by-month data summary, what to expect, what to do before a fire, and what to do during one.

How it works

  • Daily NASA FIRMS hotspot data (MODIS and VIIRS) covers South Asia. A statistical model builds a 14-day outlook from each place’s own history. It gives a confidence rating and a backtest against simple baselines.
  • The sensor sends a reading every 5 seconds. A background monitor classifies each one as Normal, Warning or Fire. It also raises an early warning when conditions are heating up fast, before the fixed limits are reached.
  • When a level goes up, alerts go out automatically, even if no one has the dashboard open. A cooldown and a call cap prevent alert spam.
  • The circular goes to people who live within 1 km or regularly look at that place. They must have verified their number or email and switched alerts on, and they can opt out at any time.

Benefits and intended impact

Fire warnings today are slow and general. This gives a specific street-level warning within seconds, and a calm, regular reminder of what to do. A phone call reaches people who won’t see an app notification. The aim is to give people earlier warning and a clear plan, so they can get out safely and call 112 or 101 sooner.

Tools and technology

Node.js and Express, SQLite, and plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Python on the Raspberry Pi. Twilio (or any HTTP voice service) for calls, Fast2SMS for text messages, and SMTP for email. Claude, Gemini or a local Ollama model for the AI writing. Docker and Render for hosting, and 24 automated tests. The demo uses simulated sensor readings, and real sensor code plugs in at a single function.

What is creative about it

  • It links satellite history, a live local sensor, radius-based alerts and voice calls in one system.
  • The AI is controlled. It can only rewrite text the system has already checked. If it adds a number or risk word that wasn’t in the original, its answer is thrown away, so it can never invent safety information. The data tables and safety steps are fixed text, and the circular still sends if the AI is down.
  • It works fully offline for demos, printing calls, texts and emails in the terminal when no keys are set.

What our team considered

False alarms and call fatigue (cooldowns and escalation rules), consent and privacy (verified contacts, opt-out, masked numbers in logs), honesty about limits (every message says it is not an official warning), low cost, and the Indian context (112 and 101, Indian SMS and phone numbers, India time).
